subject: Medisure Health: security intake and questionnaire handoff (clarifying scope)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Patel <asha.patel@medisure.com>
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 2 Jul 2026 15:07:00 -0700
Subject: Medisure Health: security intake and questionnaire handoff (clarifying scope)

Hi Asha —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Per our discussion, I’m kicking off the vendor questionnaire and wanted to confirm a few items before we submit the prefilled CAIQ/CSV to your team. We’ve attached a prefill template to speed the process.

Quick recap of what we heard from your side:
- You’re evaluating Redwood for an inference integration that will process clinical notes for downstream analytics (low-latency read primarily; some batched exports).
- Medisure requires SOC 2, a BAA if PHI is present, and evidence of encryption and audit logging.
- Procurement has requested an initial security intake and an estimate of compliance timeline.

Clarifying questions for your security and procurement folks (helps us prefill accurately):
1) SOC 2 scope: are you requiring a SOC 2 Type II for production access, or is Type I sufficient for initial testing? If Type II, any preferred rolling period (e.g., last 12 months)?
2) PHI: will any of the data we receive be considered PHI under HIPAA? If yes, we’ll surface BAA next steps and whether Private deployment (VPC) is preferred.
3) Data residency: do you need all logs/data to remain in a US-only region, or is multi-region acceptable?
4) Key management: do you require customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) or is Redwood-managed encryption acceptable?
5) Retention: expected maximum retention for request/response data and logs (default retention can be configured).
6) Subprocessors: any blacklisted subprocessors or a preferred vendor-control questionnaire?
7) Timeline: target date for completion of the questionnaire + any procurement deadlines we should be aware of.

Next steps from our side:
- We’ll prefill the CAIQ and attach our latest SOC 2 summary and SOC 2 report (redacted) for your review.
- If PHI is involved, we’ll attach a proposed BAA and flag Private deployment options.

Attaching: redwood-prefill-caiq.xlsx (prefill), redwood-soc2-report-2025.pdf (redacted summary), proposed-BAA-draft.docx (template)

If it helps, I can loop in solutions engineering for a quick 30-min session next week to show our VPC/Private deployment and key management options — does Tue/Wed afternoon PST work?

Thanks — looking forward to your answers so we can get the questionnaire into your tracker.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0134

From: Asha Patel <asha.patel@medisure.com>

Date: Fri, 3 Jul 2026 10:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Medisure Health: security intake and questionnaire handoff (clarifying scope)

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear recap and the attachments. Quick answers from our side to help your prefill:

1) SOC 2: We require SOC 2 Type II for production usage. For evaluation we can accept a Type I and a roadmap to Type II. For production, the auditors typically ask for a 12-month rolling period.
2) PHI: Yes — we anticipate some PHI in the clinical notes stream. We will need a signed BAA before production traffic.
3) Data residency: US-only is preferred; we need logs and any persistent storage to remain in US regions.
4) Key management: For production, customer-managed keys are preferred. For POC, Redwood-managed keys are acceptable.
5) Retention: We are proposing a default 30-day request/response retention for POC, with 90 days for production unless otherwise negotiated.
6) Subprocessors: We can provide a list of disallowed subprocessors if needed; for now, please include your standard subprocessor list.
7) Timeline: procurement is targeting a go/no-go decision by 2026-08-15 for this pilot. We’d like the questionnaire back by 2026-07-12 so our security team can review.

Additional notes: we’ll need clarity on logging/audit export formats (syslog vs. S3), and whether debug logs ever include PII/PII-equivalent tokens. Also: will Redwood persist model KV cache across sessions in a way that could store PHI? If so, what are the controls?

I’ll ask procurement to respond with their timeline and loop in the legal contact for BAA redlines.

Regards,
Asha
Security Engineer, Medisure Health
asha.patel@medisure.com
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Patel <asha.patel@medisure.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 6 Jul 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Medisure Health: security intake and questionnaire handoff (clarifying scope)

Hi Asha —

Thanks for the quick clarifications — really helpful. A few answers and follow-ups from the engineering/compliance side: 

- SOC 2: We can provide a current Type II report for the last 12 months (redacted) and a SOC 2 summary. Attached is the redwood-soc2-report-2025.pdf. For POC we typically ship a Type I summary if needed, but since you prefer Type II for production that aligns with our standard offers.
- PHI & BAA: Because you indicated PHI will be in scope, we’ll escalate to Legal and circulate the proposed BAA (attached). Please have your legal team mark any redlines; we can usually turn around small BAA redlines within 3–5 business days.
- Data residency: We can restrict all persistent storage and logs to a US region and will document the configuration in the CAIQ prefill.
- Key management & KV cache: For production with customer-managed keys we support BYOK via common KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS). Regarding model KV cache: by default our serving runtime keeps ephemeral KV cache in GPUs for performance and does not persist it to durable storage beyond the configured request/response retention window. For customers requiring deterministically non-persistent cache, we can enable strict no-persistence mode and additional controls in Private deployment. We will document cache behavior in the SAQ/CAIQ notes.
- Logging: Audit logs can be exported to S3 or to your syslog collector; we redact any PII fields by default from debug traces, and debug logs are gated behind a secure flag that requires explicit enablement.

Next steps:
1) Jordan will update the prefilled CAIQ with the answers above and return it to you by 2026-07-09.
2) Please route the BAA redlines to legal@redwood.ai when available.
3) If you want a short demo of Private/VPC options and KMS setup, Jordan and I can run a 30-min walkthrough the week of 2026-07-12.

Attaching: redwood-soc2-report-2025.pdf, proposed-BAA-draft.docx

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
